g.text: An EOS id is appended after every document.
Split into train data and validation data.
Corpus as one stream of token ids
Warmup (linear ramp up), then cosine decay down to 10% of the peak.
Pick the learning rate for this step
Each window of T tokens is cut from a random position:
y = ids[i+1 : i+T+1] (x shifted by one token)
Position t must predict y[t] while seeing only x[0..t].
Sample a random batch of windows
Forward pass (same weights and layers as generation)
Same pre-norm layer as the generation diagram:
The whole window goes through at once (no KV cache).
The causal mask is what lets every position be trained in parallel
Applied to ALL positions (no Slicing step):
Softmax is folded into cross-entropy: each position's logits are
compared with the true next token y[t]. All positions run in parallel.
(Teacher forcing: the input is always the true text, never the model's own guess.)
Before any training the loss is about ln(vocab_size).
Mean over all batch x position losses
For every weight: which direction lowers the loss?
(gradient of the loss with respect to that weight)
Nudges every weight a tiny bit against its gradient.
The weights are the only thing that is learned and stored.
Average loss over a few batches of train data and validation data.
Uses the generation flow with a fixed prompt and seed,
so differences between checkpoints come only from the weights.
Then model.train() turns dropout back ON.
A fork = steps that run in parallel.
